attacks.claim: go.mod adds `replace go.uber.org/zap => ../zap`, pointing at a sibling directory outside the repo. CI builds from a clean checkout, so the build either fails or compiles unreviewed local code that is not checksum-verified into the binary distributed to on-call laptops. It also overrides the pinned pseudo-version, so the stated zap bump (the JSON encoder fix) is not what gets built.

printPlan does not mirror computeBatches. It sizes batches from len(hosts) instead of len(rest), truncates with int() instead of ceil, and iterates over all hosts without removing the canary. The canary therefore appears in batch 0 and again in a later batch, and batch sizes differ from execution (e.g. 10 hosts at 0.25 gives 2 per batch in the plan, 3 in the real run). The feature exists so on-call can trust the plan before a 60+ host rollout.

attacks.claim: The zap bump is an unreleased pseudo-version with no go.sum change in the diff and no provenance. With the replace directive present, the dependency state cannot be verified or reproduced from the artifact.

Batching logic is duplicated in printPlan instead of reusing computeBatches, and the copies have already diverged. No test asserts that the printed plan equals computeBatches output for canary and non-canary cases, so future drift will also go undetected.
